blogs.title: Ultrasound First ‑ Non‑Contrast MRI Second
blogs.description:
A timely reminder that bedside transabdominal ultrasonography remains the frontline tool in pregnancy—but it can be misleading when large abdominal masses mimic decidualised endometriomas.
In this case two giant unilocular lesions were first interpreted on US alone as ovarian derangements.
Adding non‑contrast MRI clarified thick walls (+≈ 1 cm), peripheral vascularity and solid foci characteristic of cystic leiomyoma instead.
The lesson is clear:
• Bedside US guides rapid assessment.
• When lesions are ≥ 10 cm or hard to place anatomically switch straight away to T2‑fat saturated MR.
• Proper localisation determines whether surgery is needed even before pathological confirmation.

blogs.title: Interpreting CA‑125 During Gestation
blogs.description:
Rising CA‑125 values are common throughout pregnancy.
First trimester peaks average ≈ 23 U/mL, third trimester ≈ 21 U/mL.
A modest rise (e.g., over serial checks) signals reactive fibrosis or degenerative myometrium rather than malignancy.
In our patient CA‑125 climbed from 36→41 U/mL across two weeks—still below malignant cutoffs yet above physiological range.
This prompted careful correlation:
ultrasonography + MR → confirmed benign pathology 
but alarmed clinicians sufficient urgency for operative relief.
Rule'':
• Do not act solely on absolute CA‑125.
• Use serial trends alongside imaging.
• Keep malignant thresholds ≥ 35 U/mL anchored unless other red flags present.

blogs.title: When Is Myomectomy Safe In Gestation
blogs.description:
Surgical removal of uterine fibroids during pregnancy remains controversial,
and indications hinge on symptom severity versus obstetric compromise.
Key drivers were:
a) Intense pain­two quadrants simultaneously
audioely related mechanical dyspnoea;
b) Evidence of torsion / necrotic pedicle;
c) Rising serologic markers plus suspected infection;
d) Anticipated impairment of maternal oxygenation during labour.
We elected an early open myomectomy (21 + 6 wks)
and preserved coincident iliac vessels through meticulous hemostasis.
Post‐op modality relied on intraoperative fetal monitoring (continuous CTG).
Result:
at least preservation of pregnancy viability while averting imminent rupture/embolism.
Takeaway:
early every centre should develop multidisciplinary consensus documents detailing red flags dictating timing/invasive modality.

blogs.title: Delivery Planning With Huge Abdominal Masses
blogs.description:
Massive pelvic pathology poses a dual concern:
risk–vaginal fracture through scar tissue INFJ ouvrir ;
advert links interfere cephalopelvic ratio hinder descent.
With a caudal intramural tumours extending distally towards seminal vesicles,
a cesarean was elected once fetal maturity approached thirty‐seven weeks;
furthermore it avoided traversing scarred uterus transected during previous laparotomy.
Our trajectory aligns recent series showing ↓ premature birth rates when surgery precedes labour initiation
and confirms counselling patients preoperatively regarding operative scar integrity + obstruction prediction is lifesaving.
